audit_scope: Two interleaved RoboLab clients sharing one Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID behavior server

proof: One outer threading.Lock spans request authorization, the complete official inference call, and the per-cell request-counter update (lines 72 and 88-121).
A ContextVar carries only the current registered cell seed and is set and reset around the official inference call (lines 69 and 112-116).

The only mutable behavior-mode wrapper state is a counter keyed by immutable registered_cell_id; it authorizes the next request index and is not part of model input, action, future, history, or reset state.
_build_sample constructs video, action, and any history_action tensors from the current observation only (lines 490-555).
With history_length=1 and use_state=true, num_history_rows is zero; no history_action tensor or cross-request temporal buffer is used (lines 504-524).
The official RNG object is bypassed for registered requests by the wrapper's _next_seed monkeypatch; the request-local registered seed is passed to generation.
Generated actions and decoded futures are local outputs of the current sample (lines 557-600).
No reset, temporal-history, client-session, action-cache, or future-cache field exists on the service.

live_interleaving.evidence: The append-only behavior-server log alternated registered seeds 9503 and 9504 while both queue clients were active; every line retained the current prompt and registered seed.

interpretation: The two clients overlap only at transport and authorization boundaries. Complete inference is serialized, all model inputs are request-local, history_length=1 creates no history buffer, and live responses remain exactly attributed to their registered cell, seed, prompt, and reset. The overlap therefore does not create an infrastructure-invalid behavioral cell.
